Synopsis:
death--Jergal--climbs out of his sarcophagus to greet them. He has been locked inside for years by the god Helm to atone for his part in raising the Dead Three, wicked gods who are now plotting to conquer the realms. Jergal is emotionless and excessively formal, both resigned to his fate and that of others. He is here to assist the party because that is his divine oath, not out of any true desire to act. Players can attempt to goad or attack him, but to minimal effect, as he is functionally immortal. His only goal was to see their faces, so he can find them at camp later to offer further assistance.

Cluster Contexts:
- CHA_Crypt_JergalWandering.json: The party has just cleared a tomb of undead scholars and released Jergal, the emotionless former god of death, from a sarcophagus where Helm imprisoned him for years as penance for aiding the Dead Three. He appears as Withers, speaks in stiff, resigned formality, and—bound by a divine oath—offers assistance out of obligation rather than desire. His brief questions are mostly observational: he wants to commit the party's faces to memory and will seek them later at camp, though he claims not to know precisely when. Attempts to bait, threaten, or harm him have little effect—he is functionally immortal and speaks of inevitability and fate rather than altering course.
- CHA_Crypt_Jergal.json: The party has just slain a band of undead scholars in a tomb, where the ancient, emotionless judge of death—Jergal—has been imprisoned in a sarcophagus by Helm as penance for helping to raise the Dead Three. Jergal (appearing as Withers) climbs out to inspect the living; he is excessively formal, resigned, and bound by a divine oath to assist the party even though he feels no real desire to act. He asks a calm, philosophical question about the worth of a mortal life largely to observe the party and commit their faces to memory, then promises to find them later at camp to offer further help. Though players may try to provoke or attack him, he is functionally immortal and largely unaffected; the dialogue excerpts show a few possible player answers but do not exhaust all choices.
- CAMP_Jergal.json: Jergal, a god of the dead, awaits the player in camp. He is bound by the judgment of another god - Helm - to assist the players as penance for past crimes. He provides resurrection services to the players.
- SCE_Jergal_Debrief.json: Jergal's debrief at MOO after the mind flayer colony.
- CHA_Outside_Bandit_Melee_01_Dead.json: Speak with Dead dialogue with Gimblebock - the leader of the bandits who're looting the ruined chapel near where the player first wakes up. Gimblebock's answers are fragmented, cryptic. He can only draw on info that he knew when he was alive, and will refuse to speak to his killer if he recognises them. After a maximum of five questions, he'll fall silent for good.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Withers: We have nothing more to discuss. Continue on thy way, as if I were not here. (node 2)
- Withers: I must attend this place, after so many years away. We will see each other again soon. (node 13)
- Player: 'Soon' is rather vague. When, exactly? (node 6)
- Withers: When the time is proper. I do not know that hour any more than dost thou. (node 10)
- Withers: But I do know that the longer thou standest here, the farther away our second meeting becomes. (node 7)

Sample 2:
- Withers: We have nothing more to discuss. Continue on thy way, as if I were not here. (node 2)

- Player: You better not follow me. There would be consequences. (node 1)
- Withers: I had no intention of following thee. We will find one another regardless. (node 3)
- Withers: Inevitability is a wheel that turns of its own accord. (node 9)

Sample 3:

- Withers: I must attend this place, after so many years away. We will see each other again soon. (node 13)
- Player: You seem very certain of that. How? (node 8)
- Withers: The mechanics of fate would be difficult to explain to one such as thyself. (node 0)
- Withers: Regardless, it will occur. (node 5)

context: The party has just cleared a tomb and released Jergal — appearing as Withers — from a sarcophagus where Helm imprisoned him for years as penance for aiding the Dead Three. He is emotionless and excessively formal, bound by a divine oath to offer aid out of obligation rather than desire. His stated purpose here is simple: to see and commit the party's faces to memory, and he will seek them later at camp to provide further assistance, though he cannot or will not give a precise time. He speaks in fatalistic, inevitability-themed phrasing, and attempts to bait, threaten, or harm him have little effect because he is functionally immortal.
